title: Functional Post-Synthetic Chemistry of Metal-Organic Cages According to Its Molecular Architecture and Specific Geometry of Origin
content: Metal–organic cages (MOCs) are discrete supramolecular entities consisting of metal nodes and organic connectors or linkers, in addition to having high porosity and processability. Chemically, it is admirable that they are feasible to be post-synthetically modified (PSM) and introduce new functional groups, so it is to be expected that the properties will be different from those of the original compound. This is why they are highly regarded in the fields of biology and chemistry. The present work is dealing with the current PSM strategies used for MOCs, including covalent, coordination and noncovalent methods and its structural benefits. The main emphasis of the work is to show what extent and under what circumstances a MOC can be designed to obtain a tailoring geometrically architecture. Although sometimes remain unclear when looking at supramolecular systems by particularizing the design and their systematic approaches on the development and characterization of families of MOCs, thereby, our new insight about structure–function of MOCs relationships will escort to future developments.
